checked: Oklahoma State University Kappler text: Mar. 6, 1865, 14 Stat. 667, ratified Feb. 13, 1866, proclaimed Feb. 15, 1866; Art. 2 $50,000 for goods, provisions, cattle, horses, buildings and improvements; Art. 3 $7,000 damages. Matches.
Docket 225 compromise findings (OSU 369) opened: 225-B was the claim for the 1865 cession for the Winnebago, never tried, settled within Docket 225 Consolidated. The litigation breach is right.

Court of Claims, Omaha Tribe of Indians v. United States, 53 Ct. Cl. 549 (June 10, 1918), findings VIII and IX: 103 stock cattle bought in 1867 with Omaha money, 50 died, $1,666.50 allowed; infirmary of 1875, $3,127.08 of Omaha money; judgment $122,295.31.

Supreme Court, United States v. Omaha Tribe of Indians, 253 U.S. 275 (decided June 1, 1920), opened at Cornell LII: ties the cattle to the 1865 treaty's $50,000 and holds the fault lay with the agents of the United States; upholds the infirmary item under Art. 4 of 1854 and Art. 2 of 1865 as a misappropriation; reverses only the $4,560 for horses. This is a court finding of breach of this treaty.
changes: Added a court-ruling breach (253 U.S. 275, 1920; 53 Ct. Cl. 549, 1918) for the Article 2 cattle and the infirmary; status contested to broken (the checker agrees); compensation, today and plain rewritten from those findings; two sources added; audit line added.
